thread:
ana: Quick design spike: instead of flipping to global microbatching during KV miss storms, propose a "surgical degrade" that scores pressure per-tenant and enforces soft limits with a tiny global circuit-breaker. Keeps efficiency for normal tenants.

brian: I like surgical. What's the score composed of? We need cheap, local signals only.

ana: (typo) ana: Score = alpha*inflight_tokens + beta*kv_miss_rate + gamma*p95_enqueue_ms, computed in 1s windows and downsampled. We clamp and smooth with EWMA so short blips don't demote.

hikaru: Keep the runtime boundary clean: introduce ScoreProducer that emits (tenant_id, score, reason_codes). Admission API becomes admit(req, opts?) where opts.score_hint optional. Admission maps score->action enum: KEEP|SOFT_SHRINK|TINY_WINDOW|PRIO_DEMOTE.

brian: Sticky decisions for streaming sessions required. If we demote mid-stream we lose KV affinity. Admission must return a sticky token id to attach to session.

selena: Per-tenant state machine: OK -> SOFT -> HARD -> RECOVER with configurable hysteresis/backoff. Also maintain per-epoch tiny_budget fraction so TINY_WINDOW usage doesn't fragment throughput too much.

ana: Config sketch:
"""
batcher.surgical.enabled = true
batcher.surgical.weights = [0.5,0.3,0.2]
batcher.surgical.soft_threshold = 0.35
batcher.surgical.hard_threshold = 0.7
batcher.surgical.tiny_budget = 0.12
batcher.surgical.min_tokens_preserve = 2
"""

brian: How do we prevent noisy tenants from hogging tiny_budget across instances? Local decisions are fast but can diverge. Options: conservative local sticky decisions + cluster aggregator that triggers global circuit breaker if >X% tenants demoted. Start local-first to avoid distributed cache complexity.

hikaru: If we see divergence in canary, add a gossip sync of demoted_tenant keys with TTL. Keep it optional for Private deploys. Document privacy: all signals are local metrics; nothing leaves host unless customer opts-in.

selena: Observability: metrics/labels to add: batcher.surgical.demoted_tenants, batcher.surgical.score{tenant}, batcher.surgical.transition_count, batcher.tiny_window.budget_utilization. Emit trace event when action changes with reason_code. Console should surface recent demotion events per-tenant.

ana: Also emit audit events for operator overrides: /audit/batcher/overrides with who/when/tenant/mode. Add rdbctl commands: rdbctl batcher set-tenant-mode <tenant> <mode> and rdbctl batcher set-budget <fraction>.

brian: Admission contract must remain backward compatible: admit(req) still works; admit(req, opts) optional. Document semantics: if score_hint omitted, runtime uses current heuristics. Keep feature behind flag and gated in canary.

hikaru: Test plan: simulator that can spin up N tenants with configurable KV miss patterns, validate false-positive demote rate <2%, and measure throughput impact at tiny_budget 0.12 and 0.05. Also test long-stream sticky behavior and session handoff.

selena: Implementation plan: 1) Hikaru implements ScoreProducer crate + unit tests 2) Brian modifies admission signature + coalescer budget enforcement 3) Ana wires Console events and audit logs. Canary rollout for 2 weeks with telemetry review.

canary-bot: canary-bot: queued rollout -> batcher-surgical-degrade-v0.1 to canary. Logs sent to /observability/batcher/surgical.

brian: One more fairness rule: ensure PRIO_DEMOTE still leaves a minimum token allocation so a demoted tenant makes forward progress (no starvation). e.g., min_tokens_preserve = 2 per epoch.

hikaru: Edge-case: sudden global KV outages. Global circuit-breaker should invert behavior: shrink tiny_budget to near-zero to force more coalescing, reducing wasted compute and protecting throughput. We'll implement cluster_kv_spike_shrink param.

ana: We should also add telemetry hooks so Optimize can later recommend per-tenant tiny_budget or model/quantization suggestions when demotions persist. Expose demotion history per-tenant for 7 days.

selena: Security note: for Private deployments default to disabled; enable only if admin grants. Add a compliance checklist in PR.

brian: OK I'll draft admit() PR with enums and minimal compatibility tests. Keep action strings stable for futures.

hikaru: I'll build the sim harness and share tuning spreadsheet.

ana: Good session. Surgical degrade should reduce tail risk without blowing up token cost like global microbatch fallback. We'll tune on canary and iterate. :thumbsup:
